en: The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of the Holy and Supreme Lamp-Light Tathāgata,
spoken by the Buddha at the Temple of Indra’s Palace in the Kingdom of Uddiyāna, North India.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharma, the Imperially Enfeoffed Purple-Robed Śramaṇa Subject Shi Hu, by imperial decree: Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
Together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
as well as a multitude of hundreds of thousands of immeasurable humans, devas, and bodhisattvas,
he sat surrounded by them in reverent attendance as he preached the Dharma.
At that time, hundreds of thousands of koṭis of buddha-fields all proceeded to that world of Boundless Flowers,
where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Supreme Lamp-Light resided.
He manifested his body dwelling there, walking to and fro, and preaching the Dharma.
There were two bodhisattvas there:
the first was named Mahāprabha, and the second was named Amitaprabha.
At that time, that Buddha dispatched two bodhisattvas to the world of Sahā,
to the Jeta Grove in Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park,
to go before Śākyamuni Tathāgata, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Having arrived, they prostrated with their heads at the feet of the World-Honored One and sat to one side.
Those two bodhisattvas addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"From this buddha-field, we have traveled through hundreds of thousands of koṭis of buddha-fields."
There is a world named Boundless Flower.
In that land there is a Buddha named Supreme Lamp-Light Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Dwelling therein, he constantly preaches the sublime Dharma.
Because that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Supreme Lamp-Light,
has sent us to the Sahā world.
He inquired after the World-Honored One’s health, asking whether he was free from illness and affliction,
and how his physical strength remained light and agile, and whether he dwelt in comfort and happiness.
Thus he spoke.
Furthermore, all those who are humans and non-humans—
bhūtas, piśācas, yakṣas, rākṣasas,
kumbhāṇḍas, and kumbhāṇḍa army commanders.
Because of disturbances and afflictions such as royal law, thieves, snakes, scorpions,
malignant sores, insects, ants, kaṇabhas, and bhūtas.
That Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Supreme Lamp-Light,
has spoken these dharani-mantra verses;
because his fame is heard throughout the ten directions, he has dispatched me here.
For the sake of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings,
his countenance is serene and joyful, his physical marks are complete, and his body and mind are tranquil.
By the power of these secret merits, he protects and sustains all living beings.
He then spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:

*tadyathā* | *jvale* | *jvala-kṣite* | *hūṃ kama-ka* | *sama-te-maha* | *sama-te* | *maha-jvale* | *jvala-miṃ* | *sahi-sare* | *maha-jvale* | *u-ke su-ke* | *ta-miṃ sama-te* | *maha-sama-te* | *maha-samiṃ* | *svāhā*. At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
Listen attentively now.
These dhāraṇī verses are extremely difficult to encounter;
one should receive, uphold, read, recite, and explain them to others.
This Amoghapāśa dhāraṇī is likewise difficult to encounter even when a Buddha appears in the world.
If there are sons or daughters of noble family who...
By hearing, upholding, and explaining it to others,
one attains the supernormal power of recollecting past lives (*pūrvanivāsānusmṛti-jñāna*), seeing the events of one's past existences throughout seven lifetimes,
and all afflictions (*kleśa*) are completely eliminated.
One shall not experience any of one's past karmic deeds.
Furthermore, Ānanda,
this dharāṇī mantra chapter and its phrases—
Seventy-seven koṭis of Buddhas have together proclaimed it:
if any sentient beings,
upon hearing these words and phrases of this dhāraṇī, do not believe them but instead slander and revile them.
This is equivalent to slandering seventy-seven koṭis of buddhas.
At that time, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Ajita rose from his seat,
bared his right shoulder, and placed his right knee on the ground.
Joining his palms toward the Buddha, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I too shall proclaim the dharani mantra verses for the benefit and peace of all sentient beings."
By means of this secret [rite],
one protects sentient beings and increases their extraordinary power of merit, causing their physical appearance to become joyful and radiant.
Thus, he spoke the dhāraṇī:

*Tadyathā*: āṭu, vaṭu, naṭu, mahā-kuṇḍaṭu, akṣi-karṣi, anukarṣi, manakarṣi, ānanda, khaju-mahākhaju, sanne-khette-khette, tarume, dhurume, he-re mi-re ti-re, svāhā. At that time, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
Listen attentively now.
These mantra-syllables of the maṇi-dhāraṇī are most rare;
you should receive, uphold, read, recite, and explain them to others.
The appearance of a Buddha in the world is likewise extremely rare.
Furthermore, Ānanda,
if there are sons or daughters of noble family...
If one hears these dharani phrases in this way,
and receives, maintains, recites, reads, and explains them,
one will attain the supernormal power of recollecting past lives and see the events of one's past existences throughout twelve lifetimes.
One shall no longer undergo the retribution of any past karma.
Furthermore, Ānanda,
this dhāraṇī chapter and its phrases—
Eighty koṭis of Buddhas have together proclaimed it:
if anyone slanders this dhāraṇī,
it is no different from slandering eighty koṭis of Buddhas.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī rose from his seat,
bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground,
joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Bhagavān, I too shall recite these dhāraṇī verses for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings,
and by means of this secret, supreme, and great power, I shall protect all living beings."
Because it increases physical appearance and brings joy to body and mind,
he then spoke this dhāraṇī:
Tadyathā | Āke ma ke | Nairi | Nāgare | Nāhile | Nāhile | Jāhila-zaṇi | Zaṇale | Zaṇalavate | Svāhā || At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
Listen attentively now, Ānanda!
These dhāraṇī verses are difficult to encounter and exceedingly rare.
You should receive, uphold, read, recite, and explain them to others.
Ānanda, this dharani chapter and its phrases are likewise rare even at the time when a Buddha appears in the world.
Ānanda, this dharani chapter and its phrases...
If there are sons or daughters of noble family who hear,
receive, uphold, read, recite, chant, and explain it to others,
they will attain the supernormal power of recollecting past lives and see the events of their thirteen previous existences.
All afflictions are completely eliminated;
all past karmas are no longer experienced.
Furthermore, Ānanda:
This dharani chapter was proclaimed together by eighty-two koṭis of bodhisattvas.
Should anyone slander this dharani, [they will incur great suffering].
This is no different from slandering eighty-two koṭis of bodhisattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus, saying:
"I too shall proclaim these dhāraṇī verses."
For the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings,
may the merit of all living beings increase,
their bodies and minds be joyful and serene, and their fame be heard everywhere.
Possessing great power and a handsome countenance,
through this secret protection,
he then spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:

*Tantrīte* (1) *āṭu vaṭu* (2) *naṭu guṇaṭu* (3) *caṭe caṭaraṭe* (4) *taruve dharuve* (5) *raṭave* (6) *luḷe luḷe* (7) *haḷe miḷe* (8) *tiḷe siḷe* (9) *śiri saṃḷe* (10) *āpu vāpu* (11) *nāpu guṇaci* (12) *ānapati* (13) *vānapati* (14) *ke si ke si ke si* (15) *caṭe caṭe caṭe caṭe* (16) *mahācaṭe svāhā*. At that time, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
"O Emperor, listen now! Ānanda, you should receive and uphold these dhāraṇī verses;
recite, chant, and contemplate them, and explain them for others.
Ānanda, these dhāraṇī verses are exceedingly rare."
Ānanda, this *amoghapāśa* dhāraṇī chapter and its phrases are also extremely rare even when a Buddha appears in the world.
Ānanda, if there are sons or daughters of noble family...
By hearing, receiving, upholding, and explaining it to others,
one attains the supernormal power of recollecting past lives, seeing the events of fourteen lifetimes,
and all afflictions are completely eliminated.
One shall not experience any of one's past karma.
Furthermore, Ānanda, these dharani verses were proclaimed together by eighty-four koṭis of Buddhas.
If there should be anyone who slanders this dhāraṇī,
it is no different from slandering eighty-four koṭis of Buddhas.
Ānanda, if there are sons or daughters of noble family...
If one recites or chants these dhāraṇī verses beneath a withered and decayed tree,
it will be secretly protected and rescued so that fire cannot burn it;
it shall cause that withered tree to sprout branches and leaves once more, with flowers and fruits flourishing in abundance.
How much more so for those who receive and uphold it!
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the bhikṣus, saying:
"I shall now once more proclaim the dhāraṇī verses."
For the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings,
his countenance was serene and joyful, his fame spread everywhere,
his merit increased, and his physical appearance was dignified and majestic.
By virtue of this secret protection, he then spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:

*tadyathā | āṭe koṭe | caṭe caṭale | taru-pade | dharu-pade | dharu-mite | dharu-mimite | dharu-dhare | sare hare | mare mrite | svāhā*. At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
Listen now attentively.
These dharani verses are exceedingly rare;
you should receive, uphold, read, recite, and explain them to others.
Ānanda, this Amoghapāśa dhāraṇī is also extremely rare for a Buddha to appear in the world.
Ānanda, if there are sons or daughters of noble family...
Upon hearing these phrases of the dhāraṇī, if one receives,
maintains, recites, and explains them to others,
one will attain the supernormal power of recollecting past lives and see the events of twenty-one previous existences.
All afflictions are completely eliminated;
all past karmas are no longer experienced.
Furthermore, it provides protection for all bhūtas.
No devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, or non-humans shall be able to cause them harm.
Furthermore, even all malignant sores, snakes, insects, and *kaṇabha* worms cannot cause them harm;
moreover, they shall be free from all fevers caused by wind, bile, and phlegm.
Such diseases as these may flare up for a brief moment,
or persist for one day, two days, three days,
four days, or even seven days, half a month, one month, or one year.
For a long time, it cannot be harmed.
Furthermore, there shall be no such things as sores, swellings, carbuncles, abscesses, paralysis, scabies, leprosy, or skin rashes;
nor any afflictions of disease, any karmic obstructions, or any malevolent incantations.
Furthermore, Ānanda, none of all the vaitāḍas can cause any harm.
Moreover, this dhāraṇī chapter was proclaimed together by ninety-nine koṭis of Buddhas.
If there should be anyone who slanders this dhāraṇī,
it is no different from slandering ninety-nine koṭis of Buddhas.
Furthermore, Ānanda, these words and phrases of the dhāraṇī—
One should maintain mindfulness when entering a royal palace;
one should maintain mindfulness when entering among rākṣasas;
and one should maintain mindfulness when entering among lions, tigers, and wolves.
One should practice recollection when entering a wilderness;
one should practice recollection when entering a river of violent currents;
and one should practice recollection when facing the perils of water or fire.
When one is struck by poison,
or when facing any kind of fear, if one recollects [this],
none of these can cause harm.
Furthermore, Ānanda,
if there is one who upholds this dhāraṇī and should encounter an evil person wielding a blade or a cudgel, [this dhāraṇī shall protect them].
When those driven by anger and intent on inflicting harm approach,
their swords and clubs will spontaneously shatter, and they shall attain liberation.
Ānanda, as I perceive with my mind throughout the human and celestial realms, [this is so].
And among the hosts of Māras, Brahmās, Śramaṇas, devas, humans, and asuras,
if one uses these dharanī-mantra phrases for protection,
rescue, boundary-binding, and guardianship.
There is no dhāraṇī superior to this for pacifying calamities.
Why is this? Ānanda, this Amoghapāśa dhāraṇī—
Through empowerment and mindful protection, all afflictions shall be entirely eliminated.
At that time, the Four Great Heavenly Kings addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"At the time when this True Dharma is extinguished..."
We shall provide powerful assistance to that True Dharma and cause it to be widely proclaimed and disseminated so that the Dharma may endure for a long time;
we shall also extend our protection to those who uphold and maintain the Dharma.
Having dispelled all Māras,
the Blessed One praised them, saying:
"Excellent, O Four Great Kings!"
Generating courageous compassion, he protected the True Dharma.
At that time, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, knowing the Buddha's intention,
also rose from their seats and spoke this dhāraṇī:
*Tadyathā:* Vainaye vainaye, mahāvainaye, sāṃghāṇi, jñāpāṇi, ṭaṭṭaṇi ṭaṭṭaṇi, mahāṭaṭṭaṇi, kuṭu-kuṭuṇi, mahākuṭe, daṃṣṭramāle ca māheśvara svāhā. Thus spoke the Blessed One.
If there are sons or daughters of noble family who hear these verses of this dhāraṇī,
explain the meaning of those mantra-words, and receive, uphold, read, and recite them.
All afflictions are entirely eliminated;
all worldly realms attain non-obstruction,
as if upholding all sublime dharmas.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Four Heavenly Kings, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! May it be as you have wished, so that the Dharma may abide for a long time.
He then further addressed Ānanda, saying:
Listen now attentively.
By receiving, upholding, reading, reciting, and explaining the True Dharma for others,
you shall cause those sentient beings to attain great merit and fame that will be heard everywhere.
Ānanda said, "So be it,
World-Honored One.
If there are those who hear this, I shall remember it with single-minded devotion."
At that time, the World-Honored One, through the meaning of reality and by means of skillful instruction, spoke these verses:
"This dharani of the sutra was spoken by all the Buddhas of the past."
I now likewise proclaim the meaning of these mantra verses,
so that they may hear, receive, and uphold them;
thereby benefiting all sentient beings by revealing twenty-one lifetimes of various past existences.
May there be no humans or non-humans— yakṣas, kumbhāṇḍas,
rākṣasas, or bhūtanas— who create various obstacles;
may this dhāraṇī be proclaimed so that all desires are attained with mastery.
The karmic offenses of Māra and other such obstacles will naturally be eliminated;
by reciting that dhāraṇī, neither parents, brothers,
teachers, nor kinsmen shall be harmed by evil deeds.
By upholding this dhāraṇī, amidst the wilderness and on the roads,
lions, tigers, wolves, and the like cannot cause fear;
by reciting this dhāraṇī, [one remains secure] for hundreds of thousands of koṭis of kalpas.
All sinful karmas committed in past lives shall be entirely eliminated within seven days;
by explaining this *dhāraṇī*, one shall obtain within seven days the merit of all bodhisattvas,
which will not be exhausted for *koṭi* aeons.
May these four Great Kings— Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, and Vaiśravaṇa— each leading their own entire hosts,
endowed with majestic forms and divine power, constantly uphold this dhāraṇī.
May they protect the four directions and those who uphold this mantra.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had spoken these dhāraṇī verses,
Ānanda and the assembly of great śrāvakas [received them].
The Bodhisattva Maitreya, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī Mahāsattva,
the Four Great Heavenly Kings, and the devas, asuras, gandharvas, and others,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken, received and upheld it with single-minded devotion.
Rejoicing and leaping for joy, they paid homage and withdrew.
Thus concludes the *Buddha-spoken Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Noble and Supreme Lamp-Light Tathāgata*.
